name: The Goddess Provides

angles.text: As children of the stars, kaldorei inherit the direct blessings of Elune, utilizing moonlight to reveal unseen paths and concealment to blend into shadows.
Following the battle at Mount Hyjal, the night elves ended their long isolation and joined the Alliance, offering their sacred lunar powers in service of mutual defense.
Priesthood among the kaldorei is devoted to Mother Moon, channeling Elune's grace directly as guiding radiance and divine protection.

faq.answer: The Goddess Provides is an introductory rite for young night elves nestled within the boughs of Teldrassil. It instructs kaldorei in recognizing and demonstrating the innate blessings granted to them by the moon goddess Elune.

The goddess is Elune, also revered by the kaldorei as Mother Moon. She is the central deity of night elf culture and spiritual life, believed to bestow lunar blessings of protection, clarity, and stealth upon her children.
faq.q: Who is the goddess referenced in this quest?

faq.answer: Elune grants grace that can illuminate a warrior's strikes to help them hit true, as well as the ability to melt into the surrounding shadows just as the moon conceals the sun during an eclipse.
faq.q: What gifts does Elune provide to the kaldorei?

aliases: why did the long vigil end
faq.answer: The Long Vigil was the thousands of years of guarded isolation maintained by the night elves to watch over Kalimdor. It concluded after the climactic defense of Mount Hyjal against the Burning Legion, leading the kaldorei to finally open their borders.

aliases: why did night elves join alliance
faq.answer: After the defense of Mount Hyjal brought an end to their solitary isolation, the kaldorei chose to forge ties with mortal races across the sea, entering into the Grand Alliance for mutual survival and camaraderie.
faq.q: Why have the night elves joined the Alliance?

faq.answer: Teldrassil is the massive Great Tree situated off the northern coast of Kalimdor. Its high, sheltered boughs serve as the new home and sanctuary for the night elven people following the Third War.
faq.q: Where does this instruction take place?

sections.body: For millennia following the Sundering, the kaldorei maintained their solitary Long Vigil, watching over Kalimdor and guarding the sacred peaks of Mount Hyjal. The devastation of the Third War and the climactic defense of the World Tree forced an end to that ancient seclusion. Now relocated to the sheltering boughs of Teldrassil, the night elves face an unfamiliar world, stepping onto the broader stage of Azeroth by aligning themselves with distant allies across the ocean.
sections.title: A Vigil Concluded

sections.body: Even amidst shifting allegiances and new dwellings, the foundation of kaldorei identity remains rooted in the worship of Elune, the Mother Moon. Night elves are taught from their earliest days to call upon her dual aspects: radiance to guide martial strikes and clarify purpose, and shadow to cloak one's presence from enemy sight. Calling upon these hereditary gifts serves as both spiritual communion and practical preparation for the perils beyond the Great Tree.
sections.title: Blessings of Mother Moon

summary: The Goddess Provides is an introductory kaldorei quest centered on recognizing Elune's divine gifts. Set in the boughs of Teldrassil following the end of the Long Vigil, it teaches young night elves to embrace the lunar guidance and cloaking shadows bestowed by Mother Moon.
attribution: In-game quest text: The Goddess Provides
